# Gas prices by state - EIA weekly retail survey | gaspricesbystate.com

- [Gas station markup and retail margin today](https://gaspricesbystate.com/cost-stack/distribution-and-marketing/): What gas stations actually earn per gallon, how the wholesale-to-retail markup typically runs, and why convenience-store revenue subsidises fuel pricing.
- [Federal gas tax - 18.4 cents per gallon explained](https://gaspricesbystate.com/cost-stack/federal-excise-18-4-cents/): The federal gasoline excise of 18.4 cents per gallon (plus 0.1 LUST) has not been raised since October 1993. The diesel rate is 24.4 cents. Where the money goes.
- [Refining margin gas - crack spread today](https://gaspricesbystate.com/cost-stack/refining-margin/): What a crack spread is and how it shows up in your pump price. Today's refining margin and why PADD 5 (West Coast) runs above PADD 3 (Gulf).
- [State gas tax by state - all 50 ranked (2026)](https://gaspricesbystate.com/cost-stack/state-excise-tax/): State excise tax on gasoline for all 50 US states plus DC, ranked. From Alaska's 8.95 cents to California's 63.4 cents. Sourced to API and Tax Foundation.
- [Gas sales tax and environmental fees by state](https://gaspricesbystate.com/cost-stack/state-sales-and-environmental-fees/): Which states apply sales tax on top of gasoline and which add environmental fees (LUST, CARB cap-and-trade, LCFS, WA Climate Commitment Act).
- [Download US gas and diesel prices CSV / JSON](https://gaspricesbystate.com/data/): Machine-readable CSV and JSON of the EIA weekly retail gasoline and diesel prices mapped to all 50 states plus DC, with the basis and series id on every row. Public domain source.
- [Diesel prices by EIA region](https://gaspricesbystate.com/diesel/)
- [Off-road dyed diesel price today](https://gaspricesbystate.com/diesel/farm-and-off-road/): What dyed (red) diesel costs today versus on-highway ULSD, who can buy it, and the penalties for using it on a public road. IRS and EPA sourced.
- [Heating oil vs diesel price today](https://gaspricesbystate.com/diesel/heating-oil-cross-reference/): Why No. 2 distillate (heating oil) and ULSD diesel track each other. State-by-state Northeast heating-oil prices alongside diesel.
- [EIA diesel survey methodology](https://gaspricesbystate.com/diesel/methodology/): How the EIA Weekly On-Highway Diesel Fuel Price is collected: 8 regions, ~360 stations, Monday morning survey, Monday afternoon release.
- [Diesel vs gasoline price spread today, all 50 states](https://gaspricesbystate.com/diesel/regular-vs-diesel-spread/)
- [Cheapest diesel by trucking corridor today](https://gaspricesbystate.com/diesel/trucking-corridors/): End-to-end diesel pricing along the five main US trucking corridors. Where to fill up and where to wait.
- [Gas prices by state FAQ](https://gaspricesbystate.com/faq/): 12 questions about US gas prices: which states EIA actually surveys, what RBOB is, why summer is higher, why California is expensive, the federal gas tax, weekly release timing.
- [Gas price forecast 2026 and 2027 - EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook](https://gaspricesbystate.com/history/2026-outlook/)
- [Highest gas price ever - all-time record](https://gaspricesbystate.com/history/highest-and-lowest-on-record/): The highest US national average regular gasoline price in the EIA weekly retail survey is $5.006 per gallon, week of 2022-06-13. The lowest is $0.907, week of 1999-02-22. Nominal dollars.
- [Historical US gas prices by year - EIA annual averages](https://gaspricesbystate.com/history/national-average-by-year/): The EIA published annual US national average regular gasoline price for every year the agency reports one, plus the current year to date. Nominal dollars.
- [Why gas prices change weekly](https://gaspricesbystate.com/history/why-prices-change-weekly/): Why retail gasoline prices change on a roughly weekly cadence. The EIA Monday survey, crude lag, RBOB-to-CARB transition, and 'rockets and feathers' asymmetry.
- [Site methodology - gaspricesbystate.com](https://gaspricesbystate.com/methodology/): How gaspricesbystate.com sources every published figure: one federal dataset, the EIA Gasoline and Diesel Fuel Update, with the series id on the page and the coverage gaps stated rather than filled in.
